title: Interchanging the spatial arguments of coherent transformation spaces
statement:
Use universes, quasicategories, coherent functors, transformations and right-pinched mapping spaces of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], the space category $\mathcal S_{\mathcal V}$ of [def-coef-infinity-category-of-spaces], and coherent Hom bifunctors with precomposition and postcomposition as in [lem-coef-infinity-hom-bifunctor-functoriality]. Fix universes $\mathcal V\in\mathcal V'$. For every $\mathcal V$-small quasicategory $M$, the mapping spaces of $\mathcal F_M=\operatorname{Fun}(M,\mathcal S_{\mathcal V})$, formed in a containing universe, admit $\mathcal V$-small Kan models; coherent Hom bifunctors can be chosen with values in $\mathcal S_{\mathcal V}$. Let $K,L$ be $\mathcal V$-small quasicategories, and let $F:K\to\mathcal S_{\mathcal V}$, $Q:L\to\mathcal S_{\mathcal V}$ and $W:K^{\mathrm{op}}\times L\to\mathcal S_{\mathcal V}$ be coherent functors. Transpose $W$ to $K^{\mathrm{op}}\to\mathcal F_L$ and form the coherent functors
$$R_Q:K\to\mathcal S_{\mathcal V},\quad R_Q(k)=\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal F_L}(W(k,-),Q),\qquad T_{F,Q}:K^{\mathrm{op}}\times L\to\mathcal S_{\mathcal V},\quad T_{F,Q}(k,l)=\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal S_{\mathcal V}}(F(k),Q(l)).$$
Evaluation and transposition induce an equivalence of whole mapping spaces
$$\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal F_K}(F,R_Q)\simeq\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal F_{K^{\mathrm{op}}\times L}}(W,T_{F,Q}).$$
On component evaluations it sends $\alpha:F\to R_Q$ to $\tau:W\to T_{F,Q}$ with $\tau_{k,l}(w)(x)=\alpha_k(x)_l(w)$, where this expression denotes the coherent evaluation map, not merely its map on components. The equivalence is natural coherently in $F,Q,W$, commutes with restriction in $K$ and $L$, and with additional simplicial parameters in any containing universe. Empty shapes and empty values are allowed.

source.place: Agent-formulated two-variable tensor-Hom interchange based on the coherent-end formula of Kerodon Example 8.3.4.22 (03P7), read online 2026-10-17; local smallness is Cisinski, Higher Categories and Homotopical Algebra, Proposition 5.7.3 (printed p.244), which directly states local smallness of Fun(M,S) for any small simplicial set M, https://cisinski.app.uni-regensburg.de/CatLR.pdf. The displayed interchange is a transposition consequence, not quoted verbatim from 03P7. No Stacks Project tag states this quasicategorical assertion; archival copies WANTED.

proof.text: Write $E(A,B)=\operatorname{Fun}(A,B)$ for small Kan complexes. This is a small Kan complex by [lem-coef-kan-coherent-nerve-quasicategory]; its sets of simplices are small sets of simplicial maps by [def-coef-infinity-category-of-spaces]. The homotopy equivalence $E(A,B)\to\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal S_{\mathcal V}}(A,B)$ in [lem-coef-point-family-q-counit-identification] proves local smallness of $\mathcal S_{\mathcal V}$. For small $M$, [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus] makes $\mathcal F_M$ a quasicategory. Apply [lem-coef-coherent-end-twisted-arrow-formula] with $C=M$ and $\mathcal E=\mathcal S_{\mathcal V}$: every mapping space of $\mathcal F_M$ has the small Kan limit model it states. The hypotheses require only small $M$ and locally small target, not smallness of the target's collection of objects. Now [lem-coef-infinity-hom-bifunctor-functoriality], in a universe containing $\mathcal F_M$, supplies its coherent Hom with values in $\mathcal S_{\mathcal V}$. This proves the preliminary local-smallness clause before it is used to define $R_Q$.

source.place: Proposition 5.7.3, printed p.244; derivation here uses the existing coherent-end statement and the small spatial mapping-complex comparison instead of introducing another local-smallness lemma.

proof.text:
For small Kan $A$, put $P_A(Z)=A\times Z$ and $H_A(C)=E(A,C)$. Products are Kan by pairing horn fillers. On an $n$-simplex $f:Z\times\Delta^n\to Z'$, $P_A(f)$ is $(a,z,t)\mapsto(a,f(z,t))$. For $f:A'\times\Delta^n\to A$, $g:C\times\Delta^n\to C'$ and $u:A\times\Delta^n\to C$, the enriched Hom action is $(a',t)\mapsto g(u(f(a',t),t),t)$. Substitution verifies units, composition and simplex restriction, giving an enriched bifunctor $E:\mathbf{Kan}^{\mathrm{op}}\times\mathbf{Kan}\to\mathbf{Kan}$. Its fixed-$A$ action is $H_A$. In the coherent-nerve definition of [def-coef-infinity-category-of-spaces], enriched functors into a product are pairs; reversing $i\mapsto n-i$ on objects and subsets of $\mathfrak C[\Delta^n]$ identifies the nerve of an enriched opposite with the opposite nerve. Thus $E$ is coherent in both variables. Degreewise currying gives
$$E(A\times Z,C)\cong E(Z,E(A,C)).$$
The inverse evaluates $u(z)$ on $a$; both composites are identities on maps $A\times Z\times\Delta^n\to C$. Under [lem-coef-point-family-q-counit-identification] this gives the mapping-space equivalence induced by evaluation $P_AH_A(C)\to C$, including composition homotopies and parameters. Apply [lem-coef-parametric-universal-arrows] with $T=P_A$ and $\mathcal D_0=\mathcal S_{\mathcal V}$. These evaluation universal arrows determine $H_A$ up to compatible contractible choice, and give its coherent-diagram adjunction for every parameter shape. Permuting the first two factors gives
$$\sigma_{A,B,C}:\operatorname{Map}(A,\operatorname{Map}(B,C))\simeq\operatorname{Map}(B,\operatorname{Map}(A,C)).$$
On enriched models this permutes $A,B$ in maps $A\times B\times\Delta^n\to C$. Its square is the identity; substitution verifies naturality in all three variables.

source.place: Cartesian closure of spaces, specialized to the point base; explicit exponential calculation and coherent-diagram adjunction using the existing parametric universal-arrow statement. Agent expansion, not quotation of an additional theorem.

proof.text:
Here is the limit comparison needed below, derived in three equivalences. Let $D:J\to\mathcal S_{\mathcal V}$ have a limiting cone $\lambda:\Delta_J B\to D$, with $J$ small. For every small space $Z$, Step 2 and the limiting-cone criterion of [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus] give
$$\begin{aligned}\operatorname{Map}(Z,H_A B)&\simeq\operatorname{Map}(P_A Z,B)\\&\simeq\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(J,\mathcal S_{\mathcal V})}(\Delta_J(P_A Z),D)\\&\simeq\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(J,\mathcal S_{\mathcal V})}(\Delta_J Z,H_A D).\end{aligned}$$
The last equivalence is exactly the coherent-diagram clause of [lem-coef-parametric-universal-arrows]. The composite is postcomposition with $H_A\lambda$, since the first and last maps are evaluation adjunctions and the middle map is composition with $\lambda$. Applying the same cone criterion again says that $H_A\lambda$ is limiting. Thus $\operatorname{Map}(A,\lim_J D)\simeq\lim_J\operatorname{Map}(A,D(-))$ with its actual cone-leg comparison; it is natural in $A,D$ and in restriction of the cone because the three displayed maps are. We need this only for the small limits supplied by the coherent-end node.

source.place: Proof paragraph 2, mapping-limit comparison: elementary preservation-of-limits calculation from the previously established adjunction and the cited cone test.

proof.text: The transposition of $W$ is the degreewise exponential identity for internal functor simplicial sets in [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]: a map $K^{\mathrm{op}}\times L\times\Delta^n\to\mathcal S_{\mathcal V}$ is the corresponding map $K^{\mathrm{op}}\times\Delta^n\to\operatorname{Fun}(L,\mathcal S_{\mathcal V})$. Compose its opposite, paired with the constant object $Q$, with the coherent Hom bifunctor supplied by [lem-coef-infinity-hom-bifunctor-functoriality]. This constructs $R_Q:K\to\mathcal S_{\mathcal V}$, with small values by Step 1. For $T_{F,Q}$ compose $F^{\mathrm{op}}\times Q$ with the spatial Hom bifunctor: an arrow of $K^{\mathrm{op}}$ acts by precomposition with the corresponding $F$-arrow and an arrow of $L$ acts by postcomposition with the $Q$-arrow. Thus their arrows and higher simplices are specified by precomposition and postcomposition, rather than being separately chosen from an objectwise formula. Write $a:k_0\to k_1$ and $b:l_0\to l_1$ for vertices of $\operatorname{Tw}(K)$ and $\operatorname{Tw}(L)$.

source.place: Proof paragraph 2, coherent transposition before identity evaluation; construction of the two diagrams in the item.

proof.text:
Use the explicit construction of $\operatorname{Tw}$ in [lem-coef-twisted-arrow-left-fibration]. Opposite of the ordered join $[n]^{\mathrm{op}}\star[n]$ is the same ordered join with its two blocks exchanged. Consequently taking opposite and exchanging the blocks defines a simplicial isomorphism
$$\iota_K:\operatorname{Tw}(K)\cong\operatorname{Tw}(K^{\mathrm{op}}),\qquad(k_0\to k_1)\longmapsto(k_1\to k_0\text{ in }K^{\mathrm{op}}).$$
It commutes with every operator because block exchange commutes with $\theta^{\mathrm{op}}\star\theta$. Its projections exchange source and target. Also maps from that join to $K^{\mathrm{op}}\times L$ are precisely pairs of maps to its factors, degree by degree, so $\operatorname{Tw}(K^{\mathrm{op}}\times L)=\operatorname{Tw}(K^{\mathrm{op}})\times\operatorname{Tw}(L)$. These are identities of whole simplicial indexing diagrams; no reversal of the arrows of $\operatorname{Tw}(K)$ is inserted.

source.place: Index calculation for the coherent-end formula; agent verification from the degreewise twisted-arrow definition.

proof.text:
Apply [lem-coef-coherent-end-twisted-arrow-formula] first to $F,R_Q$ over $K$, and then to $W(k_1,-),Q$ over $L$. Their values lie in the locally small $\mathcal S_{\mathcal V}$ by Step 1. Use Step 3 for each small $\operatorname{Tw}(L)$-limit, with $A=F(k_0)$. This gives
$$\begin{aligned}\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal F_K}(F,R_Q)&\simeq\lim_a\operatorname{Map}\bigl(F(k_0),\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal F_L}(W(k_1,-),Q)\bigr)\\&\simeq\lim_a\operatorname{Map}\bigl(F(k_0),\lim_b\operatorname{Map}(W(k_1,l_0),Q(l_1))\bigr)\\&\simeq\lim_a\lim_b\operatorname{Map}\bigl(F(k_0),\operatorname{Map}(W(k_1,l_0),Q(l_1))\bigr).\end{aligned}$$
All limits are coherent limits of small diagrams of small spaces. The inner-end equivalence is coherent in $k_1$ and $Q$ by the naturality clause of the cited end formula; precomposition in $F(k_0)$ gives the outer diagram. Hence these are comparisons of the indexed coherent diagrams, including their cone legs, before their limits are taken.

source.place: Example 8.3.4.22 twice, together with Step 3 for the inner mapping-limit comparison; the displayed iterated calculation is agent-formulated.

proof.text:
On the coherent integrand in Step 6 apply the spatial permutation $\sigma$ of Step 2 with $A=F(k_0)$, $B=W(k_1,l_0)$ and $C=Q(l_1)$. This identifies it with
$$I(a,b)=\operatorname{Map}\bigl(W(k_1,l_0),\operatorname{Map}(F(k_0),Q(l_1))\bigr).$$
Its inverse is the same permutation. By the equivalence-and-inverse-homotopy clause of [lem-coef-coherent-end-twisted-arrow-formula], taking the two limits gives an equivalence to $\lim_a\lim_b I(a,b)$. On the other hand apply that node's product formula to $W,T_{F,Q}$ on $K^{\mathrm{op}}\times L$, and reindex by Step 5. The source of $\iota_K(a)$ is $k_1$ and its target is $k_0$, so its double-end integrand is exactly $I(a,b)$, with precisely these variances. The node allows either order of the two limits; therefore
$$\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal F_{K^{\mathrm{op}}\times L}}(W,T_{F,Q})\simeq\lim_a\lim_b I(a,b).$$
Compose Step 6, the integrand permutation and the inverse of this last end comparison. This proves the required equivalence of whole mapping spaces, with a coherent inverse.

source.place: Product coherent-end formula, Fubini, and spatial argument permutation; endpoint bookkeeping is the calculation in Step 5.

proof.text: Evaluate the construction at $a=1_k$ and $b=1_l$. By the evaluation clause of [lem-coef-coherent-end-twisted-arrow-formula], the first end projection takes $\alpha$ to $\alpha_k:F(k)\to\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal F_L}(W(k,-),Q)$; the second projects the latter mapping space to $\operatorname{Map}(W(k,l),Q(l))$. Step 3's comparison is the map of this evaluation cone. The permutation of Step 2 then takes this family to $w\mapsto[x\mapsto\alpha_k(x)_l(w)]$. Finally the inverse product-end comparison has this very same identity-arrow projection. Thus the component formula is $\tau_{k,l}(w)(x)=\alpha_k(x)_l(w)$. These are maps of the entire Kan complexes: the projection, evaluation and permutation all commute with restriction of a parameter simplex. This identifies the coherent evaluation transformation, rather than merely its values on vertices. The reverse construction interchanges $x,w$ once more and uses the inverse cone comparisons, whose inverse homotopies were retained in Step 7.

source.place: Proof paragraph 2, specification of the mapping equivalence by evaluation; explicit identity-arrow calculation for the spatial interchange.

proof.text: Each comparison above is natural in the input diagrams: precomposition by $F'\to F$, precomposition by $W'\to W$, and postcomposition by $Q\to Q'$ act on both sides of the elementary formula by the same substitution. Their composition and higher compatibility are those of [lem-coef-infinity-hom-bifunctor-functoriality], the parameter-compatible mapping comparison and the restriction-natural coherent-end formula. More explicitly, for $u:K'\to K$ and $v:L'\to L$, put $F'=Fu$, $Q'=Qv$, $W'=W(u^{\mathrm{op}}\times v)$. Restriction gives $R_Q u\to R'_{Q'}$; use this map after restricting on the left, and restrict along $u^{\mathrm{op}}\times v$ on the right. Both composites evaluate to $\alpha_{u(k')}(x)_{v(l')}(w)$. They commute coherently because restriction commutes with the same cone projections and simplicial permutation, as stated by [lem-coef-coherent-end-twisted-arrow-formula]. Write the equivalence as $\Phi:X\to Y$, with inverse $\Psi$. A family $h:P\to X$ is sent to $\Phi h:P\to Y$; the inverse is $h\mapsto\Psi h$. Whiskering the two inverse homotopies with $h$ gives the family inverse homotopies. These operations commute with every $P'\to P$, in any containing universe. Empty $K$ or $L$ gives a terminal transformation space on both sides: an empty-shape end is the point, and when $L$ is empty $R_Q$ is point-valued. Empty values require no change: $E(\varnothing,C)=*$ and $E(A,\varnothing)$ is empty for nonempty $A$, while $E(\varnothing,\varnothing)=*$. No step selected a point of an empty space.

source.place: Proof paragraph 2, compatibility of the mapping calculation and its specified maps; explicit restriction square, parameter and empty-case verification.

proof_origin.place: Paragraph 2, coherent mapping-space adjunction foundation. Online Kerodon coherent-end and Cisinski local-smallness references are checked, but no archived source proves the displayed interchange verbatim; the explicit argument is by Q25.
